chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever includes an exception in an oath, there is no sin upon him and no expiation (is due).'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on expiation for an oath if an exception is included?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), quoting Imam Ali (AS), clarifies that the inclusion of 'istitha'' (exception) in an oath renders it non-binding, thereby exempting the swearer from both the penalty of 'hinth' and the expiation of 'kaffarah'. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it distinguishes between conditional oaths and absolute ones, emphasizing that the exception must be explicitly stated at the time of swearing to be valid. The hadith underscores the precision required in verbal commitments within Islamic law to avoid unnecessary religious burdens.
